title: Lazur vs MacWhisper
metaTitle: Lazur vs MacWhisper: which one fits your Mac
description: Lazur vs MacWhisper: on-device file and meeting transcription, or a live voice assistant that sees your Mac screen and dictates. Prices from each site.
intro: MacWhisper transcribes audio and video files on your Mac and also offers dictation, all on device. Lazur is a live voice assistant: it answers questions about your screen and types as you talk.
tldr: MacWhisper is a dictation tool. Lazur is a voice assistant that also dictates.
Pick MacWhisper if typing by voice is all you need.
Pick Lazur if you also want help with what is on your screen: answers, pointing at buttons, step-by-step guidance.
Lazur is free for 3 days, then $18/month.

verdict: For transcribing recordings and meetings privately, MacWhisper is the right tool. For live help and dictation while you work, Lazur. Many people could use both.

blocks.text: MacWhisper is for recordings you already have; Lazur is for the work in front of you right now.

faq.question: Is Lazur a good MacWhisper alternative?
faq.answer: If you want more than dictation, yes. Lazur dictates in any Mac app and also answers questions about your screen, points at buttons and guides you. If you only dictate, MacWhisper is a fine choice.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur and MacWhisper together?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as their shortcuts do not clash. Lazur uses hold fn to dictate and hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask.

faq.question: Can Lazur transcribe audio files?
faq.answer: No. Lazur works live while you hold a key. For recordings, MacWhisper is built for the job.
